date_note: Date of MeetsMore's own notice (18 November 2026). It says PLAID told it of unauthorized access to PLAID's servers on 13 November and of a leak of MeetsMore customer data on 17 November.
title: MeetsMore (Mitsumoa) says member data leaked through contractor PLAID's KARTE breach
org: MeetsMore Inc. (株式会社ミツモア)
summary: MeetsMore said on 18 November that customer data it used in PLAID's KARTE for email and LINE delivery leaked. It says 60,000 people had a name, email, phone number or date of birth exposed, and 3,398,469 people only a member identifier number and prefecture. MeetsMore says passwords and card data were not included and no unauthorized access to its own systems was confirmed.
plain: A Japanese services company says customer data held in a marketing platform run by its contractor was leaked. MeetsMore says passwords and card data were not included.
exec: A breach at one marketing-platform supplier can expose the customer data of companies that link to it, even when their own systems were not accessed.
action: Organisations linked to KARTE: invalidate the linked credentials as PLAID asked, and warn customers of phishing. Affected people: be cautious of unexpected emails or calls.

evidence.quote: 対象となるお客さまは氏名、メールアドレス、電話番号、生年月日のいずれかを含む対象が60,000人
当社が会員ごとに付与している識別番号と都道府県のみの対象が3,398,469人

validation.note: Primary: MeetsMore's own notice of 18 November (株式会社ミツモア, MeetsMore Inc.; read by the follow-up run on 22 November) states both counts, that passwords, card data, addresses below prefecture and LINE IDs were not included, and that no unauthorized access to its own systems was confirmed. Cybersecurity.com relays it. A separate MeetsMore notice of 16 November concerns its own systems and is a different incident, the notice says. The wider PLAID KARTE breach is on file as a separate event.

review.note: Action said revoke and reissue credentials (PLAID asked to invalidate only) and exec said every company; fixed. 60,000 / 3,398,469 figures and fields, dates checked OK
